description: Deterministic WHO IMNCI & NHM ASHA pediatric triage rules (0-59 months) for offline edge execution.

general_danger_signs.label: Unable to drink or breastfeed
immediate_actions: Urgent referral to nearest FRU/PHC immediately (call 108/102 ambulance)
Keep child warm and prevent hypoglycemia during transport
general_danger_signs.rationale: WHO IMNCI General Danger Sign: inability to drink or breastfeed indicates critical systemic illness.

general_danger_signs.label: Vomits everything
immediate_actions: Urgent referral to nearest FRU/PHC immediately
Offer small frequent sips of ORS if conscious during transport
general_danger_signs.rationale: WHO IMNCI General Danger Sign: persistent vomiting prevents oral rehydration and medication.

general_danger_signs.label: Convulsions (current or history in this illness)
immediate_actions: Place child in left lateral recovery position and keep airway clear
Do NOT put anything in the mouth
Urgent emergency referral to FRU/District Hospital (call 108)
general_danger_signs.rationale: WHO IMNCI General Danger Sign: convulsions indicate possible meningitis, cerebral malaria, or severe metabolic emergency.

general_danger_signs.label: Lethargic, abnormally sleepy, or unconscious
immediate_actions: Check airway and breathing; position safely on side
Urgent emergency referral to FRU/PHC (call 108)
Prevent hypothermia with skin-to-skin warmth or blanket
general_danger_signs.rationale: WHO IMNCI General Danger Sign: altered consciousness indicates critical neurological or circulatory compromise.

general_danger_signs.label: Severe breathing difficulty / gasping / severe chest indrawing
immediate_actions: Keep child calm and upright; clear nasal passages gently
Urgent referral to FRU/PHC with oxygen capability (call 108)
general_danger_signs.rationale: WHO IMNCI Severe Respiratory Distress: high risk of hypoxemia and respiratory failure.

general_danger_signs.label: Central cyanosis (bluish lips or tongue)
immediate_actions: Immediate emergency referral to oxygen-equipped FRU/PHC (call 108)
Maintain open airway and keep child calm and warm

general_danger_signs.label: Stridor in a calm child
immediate_actions: Keep child calm in caregiver's lap; avoid unnecessary agitation
Urgent referral to FRU/PHC for airway management
general_danger_signs.rationale: WHO IMNCI Severe Pneumonia / Upper Airway Obstruction: stridor at rest risks acute airway closure.

general_danger_signs.label: Stiff neck or bulging fontanelle
immediate_actions: Urgent referral to FRU/District Hospital for suspected meningitis (call 108)
Give first pre-referral dose of antibiotic per ANM/MO standing order if available
general_danger_signs.rationale: WHO IMNCI Very Severe Febrile Disease: stiff neck is a hallmark sign of acute meningitis.

general_danger_signs.label: Active severe bleeding or petechial rash with bleeding
immediate_actions: Apply direct clean pressure if external bleeding
Immediate emergency referral to FRU/District Hospital (call 108)
general_danger_signs.rationale: Active hemorrhage or hemorrhagic fever requires urgent hospital stabilization.

general_danger_signs.label: Very high fever (hyperpyrexia)
immediate_actions: Begin tepid sponging and administer age-appropriate paracetamol if able to swallow
Urgent referral to PHC/FRU for severe febrile illness evaluation
general_danger_signs.rationale: Hyperpyrexia carries high risk of febrile seizures, sepsis, or cerebral malaria.

red_rules.label: Severe Pneumonia / Hypoxemia (SpO2 < 90%)
immediate_actions: Urgent referral to oxygen-equipped PHC/FRU (call 108)
Administer pre-referral antibiotic per ANM standing protocol
red_rules.rationale: SpO2 below 90% defines critical hypoxemia requiring immediate supplemental oxygen.

red_rules.label: Very Severe Disease in Young Infant (<2 months with chest indrawing or grunting)
immediate_actions: Keep infant warm (skin-to-skin KMC)
Urgent referral to SNCU/FRU immediately (call 108)
red_rules.rationale: Young infants (<2 months) with severe chest indrawing or grunting deteriorate rapidly.

yellow_rules.label: Pneumonia (Fast breathing for age or lower chest wall indrawing)
immediate_actions: Refer to PHC/ANM today for oral Amoxicillin and clinical assessment
Advise caregiver on danger signs requiring immediate return
Schedule ASHA follow-up visit in 2 days
yellow_rules.rationale: WHO IMNCI Pneumonia classification: age-specific tachypnea or chest indrawing requires antibiotic therapy.

yellow_rules.label: Borderline Oxygen Saturation (SpO2 90-93%)
immediate_actions: Refer to PHC today for pulse oximetry re-check and respiratory evaluation
yellow_rules.rationale: SpO2 between 90% and 93% warrants timely clinical review.

green_rule.label: No Pneumonia: Cough or Cold
immediate_actions: Continue breastfeeding and age-appropriate fluids/feeding
Soothe throat with safe home remedies (warm fluids if >6 months)
Return immediately if breathing becomes fast/difficult or child cannot drink
green_rule.rationale: Cough without fast breathing, chest indrawing, or danger signs can be managed safely at home.

red_actions: Urgent referral to FRU/PHC for IV rehydration (Plan C)
Give frequent sips of ORS on the way if child can drink; continue breastfeeding
yellow_actions: Initiate ORS Plan B under ANM/PHC supervision
Start Zinc supplementation (10 mg/day if <6m, 20 mg/day if >=6m) for 14 days
Refer to PHC if blood in stool (dysentery) or diarrhea >=14 days
green_actions: Give ORS Plan A at home after every loose stool
Give Zinc supplementation for 14 days and continue full feeding/breastfeeding
Return immediately if child develops sunken eyes, lethargy, blood in stool, or inability to drink

red_actions: Give age-appropriate paracetamol and tepid sponging if fever >=38.5C
yellow_actions: Refer to PHC/ANM for Malaria RDT / Dengue screening and medical evaluation
Administer paracetamol for comfort and encourage oral fluids
Follow up in 2 days if fever persists
green_actions: Encourage fluids, light clothing, and tepid sponging
Monitor temperature every 4-6 hours and escalate if fever rises >=38.0C or lasts >=3 days

red_actions: Urgent referral to Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre (NRC) / PHC for Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM)
Screen immediately for hypothermia, hypoglycemia, and infection
yellow_actions: Refer to PHC/Anganwadi Centre for Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) or anemia workup
Provide IYCF nutritional counseling, IFA/deworming evaluation, and bi-weekly MUAC follow-up
green_actions: Continue age-appropriate IYCF nutrition and routine growth monitoring at Anganwadi
